[06_how_to_claim#2]
How to make a claim. 1. An itemised receipt from the provider, showing the treatment, the date and the amount. Every claim needs one; a payment card slip or bank statement is not an itemised receipt. 2. A referral, if the treatment needs one: - consultant visits need a referral from your GP; - physiotherapy needs a referral from a GP or consultant. 3. A pre-authorisation number, for a day case procedure or an inpatient stay.

[05_pre_authorisation#6]
Pre-authorisation. Other treatment. GP visits, consultant visits, physiotherapy and prescriptions do not need pre-authorisation, but consultant visits and physiotherapy need a referral. See "Cover and annual limits".

[10_contact_and_privacy#3]
Contact us and your data. The online help assistant answers general questions about your plan from these member documents. When you are signed in to the member portal, it can also look up the status of your own claims. It cannot see anyone else's claims, cannot change, approve or resubmit a claim, cannot give medical advice, and cannot confirm whether a claim will be paid. To send documents or appeal a decision, use the member portal.

[09_appeals_and_complaints#2]
Appeals and complaints. How to appeal. Reply to the decision letter or use the member portal, and say why you think the decision is wrong. Include anything that was missing from the original claim, for example a referral, a pre-authorisation number, or a provider's description showing an injury was accidental.
